newsitem.title: USA: Corp players eye global deals amid quiet U.S. tone.
newsitem.headline: Corp players eye global deals amid quiet U.S. tone.

text.p: Amid a quiet tone so far on the domestic corporate bond front, Wednesday's bulk of new issue activity is slated to come from abroad as $1.5 billion in new global debt offerings hit the market, dealers said.

"It's a bit quiet this morning because the (Treasury) market traded down a touch but it should be active due to the global debt supply and other domestic issues currently being worked on," said one high-grade syndicate source.
So far on Wednesday, American Express Co set $500 million in 6.75 percent seven-year global debt at 39 basis points over Treasuries. Lehman Brothers underwrote the deal.
The AMEX deal priced at the tighter end of price talk, as initial talk was seen between 39 to 41 basis points, players said.

Also on Wednesday, Bayerische Landesbank GZ (New York branch) sold $1.0 billion in 6.625 percent 10-year global debt at 25 basis points over Treasuries. The deal was underwritten by joint managers Merrill Lynch and JP Morgan Securities.
The deal priced at its initial price talk level of 25 basis points over Treasuries, players said.
The deal came at its initiai price talk level, players added.

Among other foreign issuance, the Republic of South Africa is slated to bring a $500 million 20-year yankee issue via Merrill Lynch later today, sources said. Price talk on the issue is seen between 190 and 210 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, they said.
Turning to the domestic front, a number of deals still remain on the calendar for near-term issuance, but other names continue to make their way in, syndicate sources said.

One new name that has emerged is Salomon Brothers, which is rumored to bring a $300 million three-year debt offering for themselves at 60 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, high-grade syndicate sources said.
Among other issues expected are RJR Nabisco's $350 million two-part debt offering via joint managers Morgan Stanley & Co Inc and Merrill Lynch & Co, syndicate sources said.
The RJR deal is expected to include a $150 million seven-year issue as well as a $200 million 10-year issue.
Also, Toro Co is expected to issue $75 million in 10-year debt and $100 million in 30-year debt via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Old Republic International is expected to sell $115 million in Aa2/AA-minus rated 10-year debt via Lehman Brothers, players said. Price talk is seen at 60 basis points over Treasuries.
In addition, Pohang Iron & Steel is expected to bring $300 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities Inc, players said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, The North Atlantic Trading Co sold $155 million in seven-year 144A senior notes at 11 percent, sources said.
Looking ahead, the bulk of high-yield supply this week is expected to come from the private placement market, which now comprises a little more than 50 percent of high-yield issuance.
Boyd Gaming Corp is expected to issue $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers, sources said.

Oxford Automotive Inc is slated to bring a $125 million offering of 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers, sources said. Price talk is seen between 375 basis points and 400 basis points over Treasuries, they said.
Also, Echostar DBS Corp will sell $325 million in five-year senior secured notes via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities, players said.

Another $150 million in 144A 10-year senior subordinated notes will be brought by Coach USA Inc and will also be underwritten by DLJ. Price talk on the issue is seen between 9.25 and 9.50 percent, players added.
Among other 144A deals are Equimar Shipholdings Ltd's $100 million debt issue and Leiner Health Products $85 million offering, dealers said.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond is unchanged at 98-24/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
